prompt: Candid documentary photo of a real serving of nasi goreng as eaten at a small warung in Jakarta: a plate of glistening dark-brown fried rice (kecap manis gives it the deep caramel colour), with the individual grains separate and not mushy. On top: a sunny-side-up fried egg (telur ceplok) with crispy lacy edges and a slightly runny yolk. A few shards of krupuk (prawn crackers) leaning against the rice. A small pile of acar (pickled cucumber and carrot) and a slice of cucumber on the side. A small spoonful of sambal terasi or sambal kecap. A few stalks of fried shallots (bawang goreng) scattered on top. Served on a chipped plain white plate, on a worn wooden or formica warung table, a glass of iced tea and small warung condiment jars softly out of focus behind. Soft natural daylight from the open shopfront, viewed from about 40 degrees above, 35mm lens, moderate depth of field. Everyday unstyled plating, slightly messy edges with a bit of rice scattered and sauce drip, true-to-life colours, realistic textures. The rice must be dark brown, not yellow, not white, not orange. No food styling, no microgreens, no Western sausage, no Western plates, no Delft-pattern china, no fusion garnishes, no studio lighting, no text, no logos, no people, no hands.
